title: Degree as a multiplicity-weighted sum over integral components
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] with topological Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $\mathcal N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $C_1,\ldots,C_t$ be the irreducible components of dimension one [def-weil-irreducible-components], each equipped with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure (on an affine open this is the quotient by the prime ideal of the component) [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. This is a finite list; each $C_i$ is an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ of dimension one. Let $\xi_i$ be its generic point, meaning $\overline{\{\xi_i\}}=C_i$, and put $m_i=\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i}}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i})$, using the stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and module length [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Each $m_i$ is a finite positive integer. Write $\mathcal N|_{C_i}=j_i^*\mathcal N$ for pullback along the closed immersion $j_i:C_i\to X$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. With $\deg_k(\mathcal P)=\chi(Y,\mathcal P)-\chi(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ on any proper $Y/k$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle, def-pc-euler-characteristic], one has
$$\deg_k(\mathcal N)=\sum_{i=1}^t m_i\deg_k(\mathcal N|_{C_i}).$$
The sum is zero when $t=0$, including when $X$ is empty or has dimension at most zero.

source.place: Tag 0AYW, lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components, rank-one specialization; multiplicity definition immediately before the lemma.

from.place: The fibrewise ampleness-to-projectivity argument: positivity on normalized geometric-fibre components is converted to relative ampleness and then to a projective-bundle embedding. Supporting input: the proper integral curve degree criterion (0B5X). In the 0B5X proof this is the tensor-product degree formula used to pass from the degree of a positive tensor power to the degree of the line bundle and to obtain linear Euler-characteristic growth. Supporting input: the multiplicity-weighted reduction to reduced integral components in the proof of Stacks 0AYX (via 0AYW).
